name: Tu Huilong
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Haiya Group (Shenzhen) and Hong Kong Haiya Investment Ltd
profile: Tu Huilong (涂辉龙) heads Shenzhen-based Haiya Group, a private conglomerate in commercial real estate, shopping malls/department stores, urban complexes, cultural tourism, finance and hotels, with 42 subsidiaries and 38,000+ staff. A Hong Kong JP and long-serving CPPCC National Committee member (11th-14th).
interesting_fact: His flagship Haiya Mega Mall in Bao'an was western Shenzhen's first large commercial complex (~300,000 sqm, opened 2013) and hosted the world's first Burberry new-concept store.
deep_cut_fact: At the 2020 Two Sessions he proposed amending China's Property Law so residential, commercial and industrial land-use rights renew automatically, and pushed for Shenzhen-Zhongshan integration across the Pearl River Estuary.
notes: Low English-language profile; mostly covered in Chinese media. Also chairs the Hong Kong Federation of Guangdong Community Organisations-type bodies (香港广东社团首席会长) and sits on CUHK-Shenzhen board — HK civic channels may be a route. No published personal email found.

name: Madhusudhan Agarwal
current_role: Co-owner/director, Haldiram Snacks Food Pvt Ltd (Delhi branch of the Haldiram's family)
profile: Madhusudan Agarwal and his brother Manohar Lal Agarwal, grandsons of founder Ganga Bishan 'Haldiram' Agarwal (sons of Moolchand), built the Delhi-based Haldiram's snacks business. After the 2022-25 merger of the Delhi and Nagpur packaged-snacks units into Haldiram Snacks Food, the Delhi brothers hold ~56%; Temasek bought a ~9% stake in 2025 at a ~$10bn valuation.
interesting_fact: Haldiram's traces back to a 1937 bhujia shop in Bikaner, Rajasthan; the merged company was valued at nearly US$10bn when Singapore's Temasek bought in in 2025.
notes: Family is famously interview-shy (Financial Express called the brothers 'elusive'). Most coverage focuses on Manohar Lal; very little on Madhusudan personally. Best route is via the company's corporate communications.

name: Chiang Tsui-Ying
current_role: Shareholder in Largan Precision (Taiwan) via the family of co-founder Tony Chen Shih-Ching; no public executive role found
profile: Chiang Tsui-Ying (蒋翠英/蔣翠英) appears on Hurun rich lists sharing a fortune with Tony Chen Shih-Ching, co-founder (1987, with Lin Yao-ying) and longtime technical lead of Largan Precision, the Taichung-based world leader in smartphone camera lenses. Her exact relationship and role could not be confirmed from public sources.
interesting_fact: Largan co-founder Chen Shih-Ching ran R&D because he was devoted to optical lens design; both founders left the board in 2022, with Chen's son Chen Chun-ming reported as taking a board seat.
notes: Essentially no public footprint under this name; Hurun lists the wealth as shared with Tony Chen Shih-Ching (likely family, unconfirmed). Only route is Largan corporate/IR. Treat as low-priority unless relationship is verified.

name: Leena Tewari
current_role: Chairperson, USV Private Limited (Mumbai)
profile: Leena Gandhi Tewari chairs USV, the privately held Mumbai pharma company founded in 1961 by Vithal Balkrishna Gandhi (in partnership with Revlon), specialising in diabetes and cardiovascular drugs, biosimilars, injectables and APIs. Her husband Prashant Tewari runs the company as MD. She holds a B.Com from Mumbai University and an MBA from Boston University.
interesting_fact: Media-shy and one of India's richest women, she loves animals and travels into forests across India; USV bought German generics maker Juta Pharma in 2018.
deep_cut_fact: In 2013 she wrote 'Beyond Pipes and Dreams', a biographical book about USV founder Vithal Balkrishna Gandhi; she also supports the Dr Sushila Gandhi Centre for Underprivileged Women, which mentors girls in academics, dance and computers.
notes: Very private; avoids media and events. Sources conflict on whether Vithal Gandhi was her father (Forbes) or grandfather (Wikipedia) — avoid stating the relationship. Best route: USV corporate office.

name: Zhang Hongfu
current_role: Co-chairman and executive director, Mixue Group (HKEX: 2097); stepped down as CEO in March 2026
profile: Zhang Hongfu co-founded Zhengzhou-based Mixue Bingcheng with elder brother Hongchao, joining in 2007 and serving as CEO from December 2017 to March 2026, when CFO Zhang Yuan took over. Mixue is a near-fully franchised, ultra-cheap bubble tea/ice cream chain with 50,000+ stores (incl. ~5,000 overseas), listed via a $444m Hong Kong IPO in March 2025.
interesting_fact: Mixue is the world's second-biggest freshly-made drinks seller by cups after Starbucks; the brothers are described as complementary, with Hongfu the outgoing marketing/branding mind and Hongchao the introverted operations and supply-chain lead.
deep_cut_fact: He left school in 2007 to join his brother's venture, which began in 1997 as a small cold-drink/shaved-ice stall in Zhengzhou.
notes: Mixue is HK-listed; IR site ir.mxbc.com. The 'Snow King' mascot and ultra-low-price franchise/supply-chain model are good podcast hooks. Hongfu was the brand/marketing face of the company.

name: Greg Love
current_role: Co-CEO (with brother Frank Love), Love's Travel Stops & Country Stores, Oklahoma City
profile: Greg Love is co-CEO of Love's, the family-owned truck-stop and convenience chain founded by his parents Tom and Judy Love in 1964, now 600+ locations in 42 states with ~$22bn in estimated sales. He began working at the company in high school and previously held roles including president/COO and VP of real estate. Founder Tom Love died in 2025.
interesting_fact: Love's is a sizable energy-transition player: its Trillium unit (bought 2016, renamed Love's Alternative Energy in 2025) runs 100+ CNG stations, hydrogen stations, EV charging and RNG supply.
deep_cut_fact: Love's opened its first hydrogen fueling station in 2018 at the Orange County Transportation Authority's Santa Ana bus facility, via its then-subsidiary Trillium CNG.
notes: Strong energy-podcast fit (truck fuel, CNG/RNG, hydrogen, EV charging). Low personal media profile; route via Love's media group. Aggregators say he holds a BA from Trinity University (unverified).

name: Girdharilal Bawri
current_role: Chairman and co-founder, Macleods Pharmaceuticals (Mumbai)
profile: Girdharilal Bawri co-founded Macleods Pharmaceuticals in 1986 with brothers Rajendra Agarwal and Banwarilal Bawri; the family had owned a pharmacy in Jaipur. Privately held Macleods began with anti-TB drugs and is now a top-10 Indian pharma firm selling generics (HIV, malaria, diabetes, cardio, respiratory) in 170+ countries. Brother and MD Rajendra Agarwal died in November 2025.
interesting_fact: The company is named after John Macleod, a Scottish doctor and author of medical textbooks; the three brothers and their families lived together in the same Mumbai building.
deep_cut_fact: Macleods built its business on first- and second-line tuberculosis medicines and became a key exporter of affordable TB drugs; its first R&D centre opened in Mumbai in 2000.
notes: No interviews found; very low media profile. Family recently lost co-founder Rajendra Agarwal (Nov 2025) — be sensitive in timing/tone. Route via Macleods corporate office (contact page is JS-rendered; check https://www.macleodspharma.com/contact-us in a browser).

name: Lachman Das Mittal
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus/Chairman, Sonalika Group (International Tractors Ltd), Hoshiarpur, Punjab
profile: Lachhman (Lakshman) Das Mittal, born 1931 in Hoshiarpur, spent decades at LIC (agent from 1955, retired as deputy zonal manager) before building Sonalika: threshers from 1970, then Sonalika tractors (International Tractors Ltd) from 1995-96, now one of India's largest tractor makers and a big exporter. Sons Amrit Sagar and Deepak Mittal run the business; he is often called India's oldest billionaire.
interesting_fact: He launched his tractor business around age 60 after retiring from LIC, making him one of the world's most striking late-start founders.
deep_cut_fact: He holds an M.A. in English and Urdu from Panjab University, and once quipped: 'Once I applied for dealership of Maruti Udyog but was rejected. Today, I give out dealerships.'
notes: Aged ~95; operational leadership is with sons Amrit Sagar Mittal (Vice Chairman) and Deepak Mittal (MD). For a podcast, the sons may be the realistic guests; Sonalika has a media room with interviews.

name: Zahan Mistry
current_role: Co-owner (with brother Firoz) of the Cyrus Mistry branch's stake in Shapoorji Pallonji Group and Tata Sons; no confirmed executive title
profile: Zahan Mistry is the younger son of the late Cyrus Mistry (ex-Tata Sons chairman, d. 2022). He and brother Firoz inherited their father's share of the Mistry family's ~18.4% Tata Sons stake and of the Shapoorji Pallonji Group, which they reportedly co-own roughly 50/50 with uncle Shapoor Mistry's branch. The family holds Irish citizenship, hence Forbes lists him under Ireland.
interesting_fact: To reduce debt, the family's Shapoorji Pallonji Group listed its construction and engineering arm Afcons Infrastructure in a $646 million IPO in 2024.
notes: Very private; virtually no interviews. Reported to have formally joined SP Group with Firoz (neherald report, undated). Sources mention Yale alumnus (unverified). Avoid references to father's death or Tata boardroom dispute. Route via SP Group head office (Mumbai).

name: Xue Hua
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Guangdong Haid Group (SZSE: 002311), Guangzhou
profile: Xue Hua (薛华) founded Haid Group in the late 1990s, growing it into one of China's largest animal and aquaculture feed makers, also active in fry/seed breeding, animal health and farming, with ~20,000 staff and a fast-growing overseas business (Southeast Asia, Africa, Latin America). He studied aquaculture at Huazhong Agricultural University (1992).
interesting_fact: Haid is often cast as the main challenger to Tongwei in China's feed market, and has been expanding overseas into land-based shrimp and aquafeed projects.
deep_cut_fact: After a master's at Sun Yat-sen University researching fish and shrimp feed under fish-nutrition scholar Lin Ding, he worked at a Guangdong Academy of Agricultural Sciences tech company, then quit and raised about RMB 180,000 with classmates and colleagues to start Haid, initially making aquatic premix.
notes: Mostly covered in Chinese media; little English presence. Haid website was unreachable at time of research; IR contact should be in its Shenzhen exchange annual report. Founding year reported variously as 1995 or 1998.

name: John Latsis
current_role: Deceased (died 17 April 2003, Athens)
profile: Greek shipping, oil and construction magnate Yiannis (John) S. Latsis (1910-2003) died in Athens in April 2003; his son Spiro Latsis took over the Latsis Group (incl. stakes in EFG Bank).
notes: Deceased in 2003 (sources: Wikipedia; energia.gr obituary https://energia.gr/article/126902/obituary-john-latsis-one-of-greeces-best-known-shipping-tycoons-2342003). Family wealth now with son Spiro Latsis — research him instead if relevant.

name: Robert Friedland
current_role: Founder and Executive Co-Chairman, Ivanhoe Mines; Executive Chairman, Ivanhoe Electric (NYSE American: IE)
profile: Chicago-born, Singapore-based mining financier Robert Friedland built a fortune finding giant deposits: Voisey's Bay nickel (Canada), Oyu Tolgoi (Mongolia) and now the Kamoa-Kakula copper complex in the DRC (JV with Zijin), whose on-site smelter began producing copper anodes in January 2026. He also chairs Ivanhoe Electric (US copper exploration, Typhoon geophysics tech) and backs Ivanhoe Atlantic iron ore in Guinea/Liberia.
interesting_fact: He is an outspoken voice on electrification: he argues that the world's energy transition and AI/data-center build-out require vastly more copper than is being mined.
deep_cut_fact: At Reed College (political science, class of 1974) he was student body president, and he managed his uncle's apple orchard near McMinnville, Oregon (the 'All-One Farm') where his friend Steve Jobs tended trees, an experience credited with inspiring the name Apple.
notes: Excellent podcast fit (copper for electrification and data centers) and a famously talkative conference speaker. Interesting_fact is a paraphrase of his frequent public theme; verify a specific quote before using. Avoid Summitville/Jobs-era counterculture anecdotes.

name: Sheryl Sandberg
current_role: Founder, Lean In / Sandberg Goldberg Bernthal Family Foundation; co-founder, Sandberg Bernthal Venture Partners; board member, Nscale (since March 2026)
profile: Former Meta/Facebook COO (2008-2022) and earlier Google VP of online sales, McKinsey consultant, World Bank economist and chief of staff to Treasury Secretary Larry Summers. She left Meta's board in 2024, invests via Sandberg Bernthal Venture Partners with husband Tom Bernthal, and in 2026 refocused Lean In on closing the AI gender gap.
interesting_fact: In March 2026 she joined the board of British AI data-center company Nscale alongside Nick Clegg and Susan Decker, as it raised a $2bn Series C at a $14.6bn valuation, Europe's largest Series C.
deep_cut_fact: She taught aerobics while at North Miami Beach High School in the 1980s, and at Harvard won the John H. Williams Prize as top graduating economics student and co-founded Women in Economics and Government.
notes: Strong fit for a data-center episode given the Nscale board seat. Lean In's press inbox explicitly handles speaking/media requests — best route. Personal social accounts exist (X/Instagram/LinkedIn) but not verified here. Avoid references to late husband Dave Goldberg.

name: Ajay Parekh
current_role: Non-Executive Vice Chairman, Pidilite Industries (Mumbai)
profile: Ajay Balvantray Parekh is the younger son of Balvant Parekh, who founded Pidilite in 1959; he has served on the board for decades and is now non-executive vice chairman, while brother Madhukar chairs the company. Pidilite is India's leading maker of adhesives, sealants, construction chemicals and art materials, and in 2020 bought Huntsman's Indian subsidiary for $290m.
interesting_fact: Pidilite's flagship white glue Fevicol became a household name in India through decades of witty, award-winning advertising.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews found. Family-linked charities include the Pidilite Foundation and Balvant Parekh Centre for General Semantics (his personal role unclear). Route via Pidilite corporate/IR.

name: Per Sandberg
current_role: Owner (with his three sons) of Sandberg Development, Malmö; major shareholder of Camurus (~30%) and sole owner of Aimpoint
profile: Per Gunnar Sandberg inherited and consolidated the holdings of his father, entrepreneur Gunnar Sandberg, buying out his siblings. His family investment company Sandberg Development (founded 1959, formerly GS Development) owns red-dot-sight leader Aimpoint and ~20 tech companies focused on water, safety and quality of life, plus a large stake in Lund-based opioid-dependency drug developer Camurus, whose value has soared.
interesting_fact: Sandberg Development grew from 3 portfolio companies (SEK 798m turnover) in 2015 to 19 companies and SEK 5.9bn turnover in 2025, run from 'Sandberg Valley', an innovation neighbourhood it built at Jägersro in Malmö.
deep_cut_fact: In 2025 Sandberg Development and Mellby Gård's FMG Circular Invest launched a Water Innovation Challenge; the winner, SWARD, makes an energy-efficient sensor for real-time groundwater monitoring. The group also made a multi-million donation to Gunilla Westergren-Thorsson's COPD research.

public_contacts.value: lina.robekk.olsen@sbdev.com (Chief Corporate Affairs Officer, published as '(a) SBDEV.COM')

notes: Described as a 'doldis' (keeps out of the limelight); declined an Affärsvärlden interview. CEO Stefan Persson is the public face. Water-tech focus could fit an energy/infrastructure episode.

name: Larry Robbins
current_role: Founder and CEO/portfolio manager, Glenview Capital Management (New York); director, CVS Health and Butterfly Network
profile: Larry Robbins (b. 1969) founded hedge fund Glenview Capital in 2000 after Gleacher & Co. and six years at Leon Cooperman's Omega Advisors. Known for concentrated, long-held healthcare bets (famously hospitals under Obamacare), he sits on the CVS board and chairs Longview SPACs. A major education-reform philanthropist (KIPP NY, Relay GSE, Robin Hood, which he has chaired).
interesting_fact: He named Glenview after the Chicago suburb where his childhood hockey team practiced, and at the 2026 Sohn New York conference he pitched stocks wearing a hockey jersey bearing the CVS logo.
deep_cut_fact: He became a CPA in Illinois in 1991, a year before graduating from Penn's Jerome Fisher M&T program with degrees in economics and systems engineering, and captained Penn's club hockey team for three years.
notes: Glenview's website was unreachable during research; no published press email found. Accessible via Sohn Conference / Robin Hood circles; frequent conference speaker. Healthcare-focused investor — weaker energy/data-center fit. Wikipedia lists him as former owner of USHL's Chicago Steel.

name: Liu Chang
current_role: Chairwoman, New Hope Liuhe Co. (SZSE: 000876), Chengdu/Beijing
profile: Liu Chang (刘畅, also known as Angela Liu), only daughter of New Hope Group founder Liu Yonghao, has chaired New Hope Liuhe, China's giant feed and hog-farming company, since May 2013. She has steered it through the pork-price cycle by cutting costs and expanding overseas; she also controls New Hope Dairy. Hurun lists her fortune jointly with Li Wei.
interesting_fact: She ranked 40th on Fortune's 2025 Most Powerful Women Asia list; New Hope Liuhe has brought its full hog-farming cost down to under RMB 12/kg, she told shareholders in June 2026.
deep_cut_fact: She took over as chairwoman of a major A-share company in 2013 in her early 30s, a 'post-80s' heir leading one of China's largest agribusinesses; she holds an EMBA from Peking University.
notes: Gives occasional interviews (Caixin 2024, SCMP 2024). Hurun self-made list pairs her with Li Wei (fintech/unicorn link); relationship not verified here. Company has been through heavy losses in the hog cycle—keep framing positive.

name: T. Satishkumar
current_role: Chairman and Managing Director, Milky Mist Dairy Food Ltd (Perundurai, Erode, Tamil Nadu)
profile: T. Sathishkumar left school at 16 (class 8) in 1992 to rescue his father's struggling milk-distribution business in Erode and turned it into Milky Mist, South India's 'pioneer of paneer' and a maker of curd, cheese and other value-added dairy (it deliberately does not sell liquid milk). Backed by Temasek and IFC, the company's August 2026 IPO made him a billionaire.
interesting_fact: Milky Mist runs a fully automated ~55-acre plant at Perundurai processing up to 1.5 million litres a day, and has stayed headquartered in rural Erode rather than moving to a city.
deep_cut_fact: In 1993 he sent his first 10 kg batch of paneer to Bangalore in a carry bag; with no one to advise him, the team learned paneer-making by heating milk with vinegar, and he chose the name 'Milky Mist' at a browsing centre because it was easy to say and had no regional or religious associations.

public_contacts.value: te.narasimhan@adfactorspr.com (T E Narasimhan, Adfactors PR - media and investor relations)

notes: Newly listed (Aug 2026), so has an active PR/IR agency (Adfactors) — the best route. Has given several founder-story interviews; a natural entrepreneurship-podcast guest.

name: Zdenek Bakala
current_role: Investor and philanthropist; owner of Bakala Capital (family office) and sole shareholder of Czech publisher Economia; co-founder, Bakala Foundation
profile: Born 1961 in Opava, Zdeněk Bakala left communist Czechoslovakia at 19, studied at UC Berkeley and Tuck (MBA 1989), worked at Drexel, Bank of America and CSFB, then founded Prague investment bank Patria Finance (1994, sold to KBC). He built his fortune via coal miner OKD/New World Resources (exited 2016) and the BXR group, and now invests via Bakala Capital in real estate and media (Economia: Hospodářské noviny, Aktuálně.cz).
interesting_fact: In 2019 the Bakala Foundation USA gave $25 million to Dartmouth's Tuck School for global learning, at the time the largest gift in the school's history; Tuck awarded him its Distinguished Achievement Medal in 2024.
deep_cut_fact: The Bakala Foundation, set up with his wife Michaela in 2007, has funded more than 220 Czech students to study at universities abroad and has supported the Václav Havel Library.
notes: Avoid the OKD/NWR coal and housing controversies (courts dismissed major claims). Energy angle exists (former coal) but is sensitive; frame around emigrant-to-banker story, Patria Finance and philanthropy. Rich-list figures are dated (Forbes 2010-14).

name: Jorgen Mads Clausen
current_role: Chairman emeritus, Danfoss A/S (stepped down as chairman March 2022); philanthropist
profile: Jørgen Mads Clausen (b. 1948, Elsmark, Als) is the son of Danfoss founder Mads Clausen. An electronics engineer (Danish Engineering Academy 1972; MBA Wisconsin 1975), he was Danfoss CEO 1996-2008 and chairman 2009-2022, building the family-controlled heating, cooling, drives and refrigeration group; his son Mads Nøhr Clausen now represents the family. He funds science, education and sport in Southern Denmark.
interesting_fact: Danfoss is a core supplier of energy-efficiency and cooling tech (incl. data-center cooling and drives); Clausen also took a sizeable stake in the WaveStar wave-energy project.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining Danfoss in 1981 he co-founded a small IT company in Copenhagen with his wife Anette in 1978 that later closed; he flies his own Cessna Citation V, and in 2005 put ~DKK 200m into building the Danfoss Universe science park on Als.
notes: Great energy/data-center fit via Danfoss (cooling, power electronics) and WaveStar. Danfoss and the Bitten & Mads Clausen Foundation sites blocked automated access; get the media contact from Danfoss newsroom in a browser. Outspoken free-market voice (CEPOS board).
